{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Herbert J. Woodall''' was a British mathematician, known as the namesake for the [[Woodall number]]s.

In an 1889 publication, Woodall listed his affiliation as the [[Normal School of Science]] (now part of the Royal College of Science) in [[South Kensington]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Woodall | first = Herbert J.
 | date = November 1889
 | doi = 10.1038/041060a0
 | issue = 1047
 | journal = Nature
 | page = 60
 | title = How not to teach geometry
 | volume = 41}}</ref> He was an [[Associate of the Royal College of Science]], and taught physics at the Normal School from 1889 to 1892.<ref>{{citation|title=Register of the Associates and old students of the Royal College of Chemistry, the Royal College of Mines and the Royal College of Science; with historical introduction and biographical notes and portraits of past and present professors|page=184|url=https://archive.org/details/b24855595/page/n369|publisher=Hazell, Watson, & Viney|year=1896}}</ref>

==Woodall numbers==
{{main|Woodall number}}
A [[Woodall number]] is defined to be a number of the form <math>n\,2^n-1.</math> If a [[prime number]] can be written in this form, it is then called a Woodall prime. The generalized Woodall numbers and generalized Woodall primes substitute any base <math>b\ge 2</math> for the base 2.

Woodall first announced his work on factorization in a 1911 publication, acknowledging in it his communication on the subject with [[Allan J. C. Cunningham]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Woodall | first = Herbert J.
 | date = July 1911
 | doi = 10.1038/087078f0
 | issue = 2177
 | journal = Nature
 | page = 78
 | title = Mersenne's numbers
 | volume = 87}}</ref> In 1925 Cunningham and Woodall gathered together all that was known about the primality and factorization of the Woodall numbers and the generalized Woodall numbers with base 10, and published a small book of tables. Since then many mathematicians have continued the work of filling in these tables.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Wagstaff | first = Samuel S., Jr.
 | editor1-last = van der Poorten | editor1-first = Alf
 | editor2-last = Stein | editor2-first = Andreas
 | contribution = The Cunningham project
 | doi = 10.1215/ijm/1258136183
 | isbn = 0-8218-3353-7
 | location = Providence, Rhode Island
 | mr = 2076260
 | pages = 367–378
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = Fields Institute Communications
 | title = High primes and misdemeanours: lectures in honour of the 60th birthday of Hugh Cowie Williams
 | url = https://homes.cerias.purdue.edu/~ssw/cun1.pdf
 | volume = 41
 | year = 2004}}</ref>
